facts.value: Financial Outturn and Reserve Appropriation 2025/26 (item 15) to the National Park Authority meeting on 10 July 2026. A revenue-and-capital outturn report — not a treasury management report. Five-page main paper plus Appendix A (Revenue Outturn, 2 pages, £'000s) and Appendix C (Capital Outturn, 1 page, £). Appendix B (Reserves) and Appendix D (Summary of capital projects) are named on p5 but not held on disk. Prior scrutiny at Resources Committee, 5 June 2026. Recommendation: consider and note the draft outturn position and reserve movements.

Net revenue expenditure ~£6.7m; funded overwhelmingly by the Defra National Park Grant (£6.269m of the £6.745m total funding in the outturn). Meeting has passed (today is 2026-08-16). The paper as printed does NOT disclose CFR, external borrowing balance, other long-term liabilities, loan-by-loan schedule, maturity profile, MRP policy statement, prudential indicators, liability benchmark, or investment portfolio.

facts.value: NOT FULLY POSSIBLE against this paper. Ran: --find 'Peak District' → PEAK DISTRICT NATIONAL PARK AUTHORITY. --as-at 2026-03-31 → 1 loan / £228,775 / 4.7000% weighted / ANNUITY profile / matures 30 September 2031 (ref PW492373, 5-10-year bucket). Indicative settlement £231,533 — net PREMIUM £2,757 (1.2% of principal). The paper carries no loan-book table, no external-borrowing balance and no rate to reconcile against. The only treasury-adjacent references in either the main paper or Appendix A are (a) 'Central Debt Charges' at a static £32k across original budget, rolling forecast and actuals (main paper Tables 1-3, pp1-2), and (b) an Appendix A row 'Corporate Projects / VEF' with actuals £21k, £11k from reserves, £32k final deficit, labelled 'PWLB interest' (Appendix A p2).
facts.note: The £32k Central Debt Charges line is broadly consistent with a single small PWLB annuity of £228,775 at 4.70% in its later years, but does not tie exactly on a naive annuity payment back-solve (£32k p.a. total service on £228,775 at 4.70% implies ~8-9 years remaining; our recorded maturity of 30 Sept 2031 gives ~5.5 years remaining at 31 March 2026). The £32k line likely also carries any MRP charge, which the paper does not break out separately. This is 'reconciles by presence, not by number' — the paper acknowledges PWLB interest exists; our file agrees one PWLB loan exists; there is no printed loan-book table to match count/principal/rate against. Internal only — do not raise.

facts.value: Defra revenue grant reduced to £6.2m for 2025/26 (-£0.6m / -8.2% YoY). Defra approved a £1.6m capital grant to mitigate, restricted to invest-to-save, revenue-generation and 30-by-30. The Authority modelled scenarios on the reduced core-grant baseline and announced a further organisational restructure in October 2025 because on that baseline it 'could not balance its budget from 2026/27 onwards'.
facts.note: Organisational-change redundancy costs of £701k in-year were funded from a mix of project income (£50k), surplus interest (£176k), early exiters (£63k), corporate overhead (£42k), budget surpluses (£47k), residual contingency (£115k) and reserves (£208k), leaving nil unfunded (p3 'Summary of redundancies and funding'). This is a funding/restructure narrative, not a treasury narrative.

summary.text:
Item 15 to the Peak District National Park Authority meeting on 10 July 2026 is a Financial Outturn and Reserve Appropriation report for 2025/26 — a revenue-and-capital outturn, not a treasury management report. The Authority is a National Park Authority under the Environment Act 1995 rather than a principal council; net revenue expenditure is ~£6.7m and the Defra National Park Grant supplies £6.269m of the £6.745m total funding. Draft actual surplus for the year is £50k, moved to the General Reserve, which closes at £425k.

The paper as printed does not disclose CFR, external borrowing balance at 31/03/2026, other long-term liabilities, a loan-by-loan schedule, maturity profile, MRP policy, prudential indicators, liability benchmark or investment portfolio. The only treasury-adjacent references are a static £32k 'Central Debt Charges' line running unchanged across original budget, rolling forecast and draft actuals (main paper Tables 1-3), and a single Appendix A row (Corporate Projects, VEF) with actuals £21k, £11k reserves transfer, £32k final deficit, labelled simply 'PWLB interest'. On the investment side, Interest on Balances came in at £476k against a £300k budget, and the £176k surplus was recycled to fund organisational-change redundancy costs of £701k; the paper attributes the lift to 'tighter management around cashflow, working to retain high cash balances' despite Bank Rate cuts in-year. No counterparty, tenor or rate is disclosed.

Reconciliation against our PWLB file is not fully possible against this paper. price_book.py --find 'Peak District' returns PEAK DISTRICT NATIONAL PARK AUTHORITY; at 31 March 2026 we hold 1 PWLB loan of £228,775 at a weighted 4.7000%, annuity profile, maturing 30 September 2031 (indicative settlement £231,533, net premium £2,757 = 1.2% of principal — indicative only, DMO binding). The paper carries no loan-book table to match count, principal or rate against; the £32k debt-charge line is broadly consistent with an all-in service on a single small annuity in its later years but does not tie exactly on a naive back-solve, and likely also carries any MRP charge which the paper does not break out separately. The balance-sheet identity (CFR minus external borrowing minus other long-term liabilities equals internal borrowing) cannot be checked from this paper because none of the three inputs is disclosed.

No email drafted. This is a revenue-and-capital outturn from a very small statutory body carrying one small PWLB annuity in our file. There is no maturity profile, no MRP policy, no liability benchmark, no LOBO exposure, no prudential-indicator breach, no rate assumption to test, no adviser's forecast to price against, and no loan-book table to open on. Leading with a £32k debt-charge line or a £229k annuity would be padded, and the comparators the platform normally offers (per-loan schedule, refinancing concentration, break-cost engine) are meaningless at this scale for a body of this type. Revisit if a Peak District Treasury Management Outturn Report, Treasury Management Strategy Statement, or the 2025/26 Statement of Accounts (audited version due to Members November 2026) surfaces on Drive or ModernGov — those would be the papers that could carry a hook.
